CausalChain: Hypoxia leads to HIF activation -> HIF upregulates glycolytic enzymes -> Elevated glycolysis increases lactate production -> Lactate is exported into the tumor microenvironment -> Extracellular lactate activates the GPR81 receptor on tumor and immune cells -> GPR81 activation mediates nuclear translocation of TAZ and upregulation of PD-L1 -> Elevated PD-L1 promotes T cell exhaustion and immune evasion -> Enhanced immunosuppression drives HCC progression.
Hypothesis: Inhibition of the lactate receptor GPR81 can interrupt the lactate-induced PD-L1 upregulation pathway and, when combined with immune checkpoint inhibitors, restore CD8⁺ T cell function and overcome immunosuppression, thereby countering drug resistance in hypoxic hepatocellular carcinoma.
Abstract: Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) is characterized by the hypoxic tumor microenvironment and associated metabolic reprogramming that contribute to therapeutic resistance. Among the metabolic alterations, enhanced glycolysis leads to increased lactate production. This lactate not only modulates tumor cell metabolism but also drives immunosuppression by enhancing PD‐L1 expression through activation of its receptor, GPR81. We propose a novel therapeutic strategy that targets this lactate sensing pathway to restore anti‐tumor immune function. Here, we hypothesize that blockade of GPR81, when combined with immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs), can disrupt lactate‐mediated immunosuppression and enhance CD8⁺ T cell activity in hypoxic HCC. This strategy has the potential to overcome both TKI and ICI resistance arising from hypoxia‐induced metabolic reprogramming.
